messages.author: 51ea28fc190ac537
messages.subject: Re: Strange behaviour with Survival analysis
parts:
On 5 February 2010 10:47, David Winsemius <dwins...@comcast.net> wrote:
> On Feb 4, 2010, at 2:16 PM, danielem wrote:
>
>> Dears RattleRs,
>>
>> fitting a survival model with cox, I obtain scores with values bigger
>> than 1.x, eg. 1.023....
>
> What do you mean by "scores"?

I think "score" means you apply a model to a dataset with the Score
option of the Evaluate tab. This uses the predict function
(predict.coxph) underneath.

The default "predict" in Rattle is with type="risk". Interpret the
risk as relative to 1. So a risk score above 1 is a higher risk than
the average in the population and below 1 is a lower risk than the
average in the population.

Regards,
Graham
